newsitem.title: CANADA: Stampeder will scrap issue if price drops.
newsitem.headline: Stampeder will scrap issue if price drops.

text.p: Stampeder Exploration Ltd, which took a drubbing in the stock market on Monday, will scrap plans to issue shares if its price drops too far, Stampeder Chief Executive Jeff Tonken said on Tuesday.
The company had not decided, however, how far the company's stock price must fall before the offering is pulled, Tonken said at the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers investment symposium.
"We haven't made that decision (on how low the stock must drop)," he told reporters. "But we think it's going up from here, not down."
Stampeder shares fell 0.55 to 5.35 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday on 2.6 million shares. Sellers included one holder that unloaded a 1.2 million share block.

"We had a shareholder that was dissatisfied that we were doing the equity issue and just took whatever bid he could get," Tonken said. He added that he did not know who sold out, but said it was a major Stampeder holder.
Stampeder was up 0.05 to 5.40 in Toronto at midday today.
The company's shares on the New York Stock Exchange were up 1/8 to 4.

Stampeder, which made three big corporate acquisitions last year, said last week it planned to issue 24 million shares to fund an increase in capital spending to C$245 million from C$160 million, directed mostly to heavy oil development.

Tonken said Stampeder had committed lines of credit in place to fund the capital budget increase, but also said he did not want to expose the company's shareholders to higher debt levels to fund the extra spending.
"You walk a fine line," he said. "You've got to determine how much equity you want and how much debt you're going to take and we'll just see where it gets to in 10 days when we do the pricing."
He said he expected big demand for Stampeder stock in the United States and was hopeful Canadian shareholders would give it the market support needed to make the issue a success.
"We want Canadian shareholders to support the stock during the process, not just dump it," he said.
Tonken said he believed the extra production and cash flow gained from the new spending would more than make up for the stock dilution.
Company executives were set to start an extended road show through the United States later today and the issue was expected to be priced on June 26.
